newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FORECAST - Nedlloyd seen hit by weak Q4.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Nedlloyd seen hit by weak Q4.

text.p: A weak final quarter will drag down full year profits of Dutch shipping and transport group Koninklijke Nedlloyd Group NV, analysts say.

Forecasts for the full year net profit excluding extraordinary items ranged from 20 million guilders to 38 million guilders, down from 49 million in 1995. Nedlloyd will publish its figures on Thursday.
Analysts expect the company's ocean shipping division to have picked up from a loss-making first half, although largely because of a healthy third quarter performance.
"There will have been some improvement in the second half, but more to do with volumes than pricing," said Pieter van Gelder of Delta Lloyd Bank.
Ocean shipping continued to suffer from poor tariffs, particularly in the last few months.
"We've seen further erosion in Q4. On Europe-Far East routes, tariffs were down three percent, making them 11 percent lower for the whole year," said Andre Mulder of BZW.
The European Transport and Distribution division has improved, analysts said, but the fourth quarter is traditionally a weak one for the sector.
Neddrill made no contribution after the completion of its sale to Noble Drilling Corp at the end of the second quarter.
Nedlloyd will also miss any earnings made by North Sea Ferries after the sale of its 50 percent stake to P&O.
For some, however, the results are of little importance, overshadowed by the company's merger of its container shipping business with Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Company .

"Nobody is really interested in the results. What matters is the strategy for the future with P&O. What we want to know is how is the merger going and how are tariffs," said Gert Jochems of NIB Securities.
"1996 was a transition year. What is important is the outlook for the sector and the company," said Van Gelder.
Overcapacity in the container shipping business will remain a problem and may eat into cost savings related to the merger.
"Capacity is likely to grow 19 percent in 1997 and 1998, while demand growth is only likely to be about seven percent per year," said BZW's Mulder.
